Part_A.title: Addressing S6 Stress: A Proposal for 'Wellness Week'
Part_A.instructions: Write a formal letter in about 200 words.
Part_A.situation: You have noticed that many S6 students are suffering from extreme stress and 'burnout' as the public exams approach. You want to write to the Head of Year proposing a 'Wellness Week' to help students rebalance.
requirements: Describe the physical and mental symptoms of 'burnout' you have observed among your peers.
Explain how a 'Wellness Week' (e.g., workshops, no-homework days) would benefit student performance in the long run.
Suggest one specific session that focuses on 'valuing rest' over 'constant achievement'.
format_guides: Address it to 'The Head of Year 12/S6'.
Use a respectful and concerned tone.

Part_B.question: The 'Overtraining' Epidemic: When the pursuit of 'Faster, Higher, Stronger' leads to career-ending burnout.
requirements: Explain the science behind 'overtraining syndrome' and how it differs from normal fatigue.
Discuss the 'Winner-Takes-All' pressure in professional sports that makes athletes ignore pain.
Give advice to young athletes on how to 'listen to their body' while still being competitive.

Part_B.question: A scene where a 'Type A' perfectionist student is confronted by their 'Chill' best friend after staying up for 72 hours straight.
requirements: Use dialogue to show the 'Type A' character's frantic, disjointed thought process.
Include a 'breaking point' where the perfectionist realizes they can't sustain this pace.
Provide stage directions that reflect the claustrophobic, intense atmosphere of a late-night study session.

Part_B.question: A story about a person who suddenly loses the ability to 'do' anything—their body simply refuses to move until they learn how to rest.
requirements: Describe the 'Great Pause': the moment the protagonist's body 'shuts down'.
Show the protagonist's initial frustration and their slow transition to appreciating silence and stillness.
End the story with the protagonist 'restarting' their life with a completely different set of priorities.

Part_B.question: The 'Glorification of Busyness' on Social Media: Why 'Hustle Porn' is a dangerous lie.
requirements: Identify the 'Hustle Culture' tropes (e.g., 'Rise and Grind', 'sleep is for the weak') and why they are toxic.
Discuss how influencers hide the 'unseen support' (money, staff) that allows them to appear constantly productive.
Provide three 'Authentic Rest' challenges for your followers (e.g., a digital detox).

Part_B.question: The '996' and 'Burnout' Culture: Why East Asian cities are facing a mental health crisis.
requirements: Define 'Hustle Culture' in the context of high-pressure cities like Hong Kong or Tokyo.
Discuss the impact on birth rates and family life when 'work is everything'.
Suggest one systemic change (e.g., 'Right to Disconnect' laws) to protect worker well-to-being.

Part_B.question: 'That 'Quiet Quitting' is a healthy response to an exploitative work culture.'
requirements: Define 'Quiet Quitting' (doing only what is in the job description) for the debate.
Argue that it is an act of 'self-preservation' against 'unpaid overwork'.
Rebut the claim that 'Quiet Quitting' shows a lack of ambition or character.

Part_B.question: A report on the 'Quiet Quitting' phenomenon in your local office and its impact on team morale.
requirements: Identify the 'root causes' of why employees are disengaging (e.g., lack of recognition, stagnant wages).
Discuss the difference between 'lazy' workers and those who are 'reclaiming their boundaries'.
Recommend three ways management can 're-engage' staff without resorting to pressure.

Part_B.question: A review of a song or poem that addresses the 'Rat Race' or the 'Weight of Expectation'.
requirements: Identify the central metaphor used for the 'Rat Race' (e.g., a wheel, a tide, a heavy stone).
Discuss how the work's rhythm (e.g., fast and repetitive vs. slow and weary) reflects the theme.
Explain why this work is an 'anthem' for anyone feeling overwhelmed by modern life.
